strategy.summary: Reproduce the Angle.to_string double-rounding and early-carry bug by building astropy from source at the buggy commit bdd570d53507, applying the developer's test diff, and running the two new parametrized tests in astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py. The bug is pure-Python float formatting, so no special platform or toolchain is expected, but the build must be from source because the PyPI wheel is not the buggy revision.

pinned_because: astropy is not pinned by any documented constraint; the buggy commit is pinned by checking out bdd570d53507 rather than by a version number

numpy has no documented or era constraint; the unpinned latest release compatible with the chosen Python is used because the defect does not depend on the numpy version (builtin round is used in the fixed path)
python 3.12 is chosen by this strategy, not stated by the evidence; it is a modern version that current astropy supports

strategy.reproducing_test: astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py::test_sexagesimal_seconds_round_at_half_a_unit and astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py::test_sexagesimal_degrees_round_once (parametrized cases, including 1d2m59.49999s at precision 0 and 285d29m41.76s with fields=1)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision bdd570d53507 with the test diff applied, the parametrized cases that include 1d2m59.49999s at precision 0 (expected 1d02m59s, buggy 1d03m00s) and 285d29m41.76s at fields=1 (expected 285d, buggy 286d) fail with AssertionError. On the fixed revision (the PR 20229 change applied on top of bdd570d53507), all parametrized cases of both tests pass, giving exit status 0.
risks: The PyPI wheel (pip install astropy) is a released version, not the buggy commit; the strategy builds from source at bdd570d53507 so the defect is present. Using the wheel would not reproduce the failure.

The numpy version is not stated by the evidence and no constraint exists; the chosen unpinned numpy may differ from the one in which the bug was observed. The fixed code uses builtin round, so the transition should not depend on numpy's tie-breaking, but this is not confirmed.
The evidence does not state dtype of inputs or outputs; the test uses Python float string parsing and string comparison, so dtype dependence is unconfirmed but not expected.

Tie-breaking: the new test includes values exactly at half a unit (e.g. 1d2m59.5s at precision 0). Builtin round uses round-half-to-even on binary floats; a NumPy-based reproduction could differ, so the test must be run as written.
If pytest imports an installed astropy from site-packages instead of the editable build, the buggy or fixed behaviour will not be exercised; confirm astropy.__file__ points into the checkout.

No architecture or sanitiser dependence is evidenced; the bug is in pure-Python formatting, so it should transition on any standard Linux x86_64 build. Other tests in the file may fail for unrelated environment reasons and are excluded by -k.

oracle.reference_source: astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py new tests in the PR diff, plus docs/changes/coordinates/20227.bugfix.rst changelog
oracle.why: Angle.to_string returns strings compared with ==, so the oracle is exact string equality with no numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion compares the returned string to the expected string; on bdd570d53507 the early carry gives '1d03m00s' instead of '1d02m59s' for the 59.49999s case, and the fields=1 double rounding gives '286d' instead of '285d', so AssertionError is raised for those parametrized cases.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the check round(seconds, ndp) >= 60.0 and minutes+seconds/60 comparison produce '1d02m59s' and '285d' for these inputs, and all parametrized cases of both new tests match their expected strings.
